body.x: QUAZAR Co., Ltd. (CEO Myunghyun Kim), a South Korean vision artificial intelligence enterprise, will exhibit at the Singapore FinTech Festival 2026, held from November 18 to 20 at Singapore EXPO. The company will showcase its proprietary platform, “QUAZAR Tagless DPP,” recognized as a CES 2027 Innovation Awards Honoree in the Enterprise Tech category. Built to address the European Union’s Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR), the platform delivers end-to-end authentication and lifecycle tracking for consumer goods without requiring physical QR codes, RFID, or NFC tags.

Founded in June 2020 and headquartered in Bupyeong, Incheon, QUAZAR develops advanced computer vision technologies that identify microscopic product characteristics from standard photographic images. Expanding beyond industrial vision, the company has commercialized solutions spanning luxury goods authentication, digital product passports, and AI-driven bird deterrence systems. In 2025, QUAZAR recorded KRW 824 million in revenue and has secured KRW 600 million in cumulative Seed and Pre-A venture funding. Its R&D growth has been backed by national technology initiatives, including South Korea’s TIPS R&D program in 2024, the government startup commercialization program in 2025, Incheon Airport’s startup acceleration project in 2026, and designation as a Global IP Star Company. The enterprise holds four registered patents, has five pending applications, and is an active member of the Korea Intellectual Property Protection Agency’s anti-counterfeiting technology council.

The core highlight presented at SFF 2026, QUAZAR Tagless DPP, introduces a non-invasive identity-capture method that recognizes products directly by their intrinsic physical attributes. The system extracts a unique visual signature from natural manufacturing traces, such as stitching patterns, tooling impressions, and leather or textile grains. Authenticity is validated through a three-stage cross-verification engine combining a vision-language model (VLM), CLIP-Hash visual fingerprint matching, and an algorithmic decision layer modeled on expert appraisal methodologies. An integrated Explainable AI (XAI) module provides transparent rationales for each decision and, in the event of cross-model discrepancies, is backed by human specialist intervention. The platform’s authentication precision ranged from 94.5% to 95.7% in testing certified by the Korea Laboratory Accreditation Scheme (KOLAS).

Verified product records are minted directly on the Polygon Layer-2 blockchain as non-transferable Soulbound Tokens (SBTs), with the underlying evidence securely distributed across the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) to ensure permanent, decentralized data availability. Over a product’s full lifecycle, subsequent events—such as secondary resale, professional repairs, and end-of-life recycling—are appended as linked tokens to the original passport. This architecture enables luxury, fashion, and footwear brands to comply seamlessly with EU ESPR take-back mandates and circularity disclosures via standard APIs and an enterprise console, eliminating the need to construct bespoke IT infrastructure.

body.x: QUAZAR enters the Singapore exhibition with expanding international business momentum. The company has engaged with global technology platforms, securing selection for the Google Cloud startup program in 2025 and Oracle’s global collaboration cohort in 2026. In the luxury resale sector, QUAZAR executed a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and a letter of intent (LOI) with a United Kingdom-based resale platform, a commercialization NDA with a Canadian partner, and is currently pursuing PCT international patent applications in the United States, the European Union, and Japan. Demonstrating municipal and industrial versatility, QUAZAR also presented its AI solutions at the Smart City Expo World Congress (SCEWC) 2026 in Barcelona, holding consultations with 29 public and corporate entities from 15 countries—including Barcelona City Council, the City of Luxembourg, Enel, and Repsol—which led to joint research discussions with a German research institute and business follow-ups in Saudi Arabia and the United States.

At Singapore EXPO, QUAZAR will demonstrate live end-to-end workflows spanning on-site item authentication, immediate SBT issuance, and mobile verification. The company is actively targeting business meetings with Asian luxury resale marketplaces, regional blockchain ecosystem partners, fintech institutions, and venture investors, aiming to execute three letters of intent and finalize its first paid international pilot deployment. Leveraging Singapore as an operational bridgehead in Asia, QUAZAR plans to establish the market references needed to accelerate enterprise rollouts across the European Union in 2027, helping international fashion exporters meet mandatory European digital product passport requirements.
